bottom_line: Empagliflozin 10 mg daily versus placebo after acute myocardial infarction did not significantly lower the risk of first hospitalization for heart failure or death from any cause (hazard ratio, 0.90; 95% CI, 0.76 to 1.06).
implications: The reported hazard ratio for the primary composite outcome (0.90; 95% CI, 0.76 to 1.06; P = 0.21) does not support a statistically significant reduction in first hospitalization for heart failure or death from any cause with empagliflozin versus placebo in this trial, while the reported component outcome shows fewer first hospitalizations for heart failure with empagliflozin (hazard ratio, 0.77; 95% CI, 0.60 to 0.98) and similar all-cause death (hazard ratio, 0.96; 95% CI, 0.78 to 1.19).

major_points.text: Event-driven, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial assigning empagliflozin 10 mg daily versus placebo within 14 days after admission.
major_points.quote: In this event-driven, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial, we assigned, in a 1:1 ratio, patients who had been hospitalized for acute myocardial infarction and were at risk for heart failure to receive empagliflozin at a dose of 10 mg daily or placebo

major_points.text: Primary end point was time to first hospitalization for heart failure or death from any cause.
major_points.quote: The primary end point was a composite of hospitalization for heart failure or death from any cause as assessed in a time-to-first-event analysis.
